Who we are 

We simplify wealth creation. Founded in 2014 in Vienna, Austria by Eric Demuth, Paul Klanschek and Christian Trummer, we’re here to help people trust themselves enough to build their financial freedom — for now and the future. Our user-friendly, trade-everything platform empowers both first-time investors and seasoned experts to invest in the cryptocurrencies, crypto indices, stocks*, precious metals and commodities* they want — with any sized budget, 24/7. Our global team works across different cultures and time zones, bringing our products to more than 7 million customers, making us one of Europe’s safest and most secure platforms that powers modern investing.

Headquartered in Austria but operating across Europe, our products are built by fast-moving, talented, “roll-up-your-sleeves-and-make-it-happen” kind of people. It’s these diverse perspectives and innovative minds operating as ONE TEAM that keep Bitpanda at the cutting edge of our industry. So if you’re someone who thinks big, moves fast and wants to make an impact right from day one, then get ready to join our industry-changing team. Let’s go!

Your mission

As a Senior Product Manager at Bitpanda, you will take end-to-end ownership of key product areas and strategic pillars, scaling our offerings for financial institutions, banks, and strategic partners. Operating in a high-impact, complex, and regulated environment, you will define product strategy, shape the roadmap, and act as a key sparring partner to Product Leadership.

You will work closely within a collaborative structure, allowing you to focus deeply on product architecture, scalability, and technical execution while leveraging client-facing insights to inform your roadmap. This is a global, fast-paced role requiring seamless context-switching across markets, products, and evolving regulatory frameworks.

What you'll do

  • Take end-to-end ownership of core product pillars, defining the long-term vision, strategy, and execution roadmap in close alignment with Product Leadership.
  • Partner with Engineering to translate complex market and partner needs into clear, actionable, and scalable technical capabilities.
  • Work closely with Client Solution Leads—and engage directly with external partners when needed—to weigh client-specific requests against long-term platform scalability and strategic priorities.
  • Proactively integrate fintech and financial services regulatory requirements into the product lifecycle, collaborating closely with Compliance and Legal to ensure every launch meets global standards.
  • Act as a central connector across Engineering, Sales, Client Solutions, Legal, and Compliance, managing senior stakeholders and driving clarity amid ambiguity and shifting priorities.

Who you are

  • Proven track record managing B2B and/or B2B2C products within finance, banking, fintech, or crypto.
  • Demonstrated experience operating as a Senior Product Manager or Lead Product Manager, with end-to-end ownership of complex products.
  • Solid understanding of regulatory requirements in fintech or financial services, with hands-on experience shipping compliant products in highly regulated environments.
  • Ability to partner effectively with engineering teams, break down technical trade-offs, and build scalable, platform-level solutions rather than one-off customisations.
  • Comfortable thinking globally, switching contexts rapidly across multiple product pillars, and navigating evolving priorities in a dynamic environment.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to align senior internal stakeholders and engage credibly with institutional partners when required.

What’s in it for you

  • Flexibility to work where you thrive – Enjoy the freedom of our Hybrid working model, combining onsite collaboration and remote work, with an additional 25 days per year to work from a city or country of your choice.
  • Reward for your impact – Receive a competitive total compensation package aligned with Bitpanda’s pay-for-impact policy, including participation in our stock option plan.
  • Support for your mental wellbeing – Access confidential coaching, counselling, and mental health resources whenever you need them through OpenUP.
  • Time to recharge – On top of your standard annual leave, prioritise your wellbeing in 2027 with 3 additional days of paid time off to rest, reset, and recharge, available once you’ve been with us for 6 months.
  • Continuous learning and growth – Grow your skills and stay ahead in your career with unlimited access to Udemy’s library of online courses at your own pace.
  • Exclusive perks and rewards – Enjoy discounts, rewards, and perks from partners worldwide across lifestyle, wellness, tech, and travel.
  • Support during life milestones – Take advantage of up to 8 additional weeks of gender-neutral new parent leave to welcome and bond with your new addition to the family.
  • Fuel and focus on-site – Pandas in Vienna, Bucharest, Barcelona, and Berlin can enjoy free onsite dining, with freshly prepared lunches and snacks to keep you fueled and focused all day long.
  • Recognition for your contributions – Celebrate milestones and achievements with recognition and rewards for your Tenure at Bitpanda.
  • Show your Bitpanda pride – Access exclusive Bitpanda-branded merchandise and gear to represent.
  • Connect and celebrate with your team – Join unforgettable company events, from our Winter Party in Vienna to gatherings worldwide, fostering fun, connection, and celebration

       .…and even more location-specific benefits designed to make life at Bitpanda even more rewarding wherever you are.

Above all, you will have the opportunity to learn and grow as part of Bitpanda’s incredible journey towards being Europe’s future #1 investment platform.

Bitpanda is committed to fostering a fair and equal environment based on trust and mutual respect. We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace is paramount to our success and we are committed to building a team that represents a wide variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Global Payments Performance Team identifies payment optimisation opportunities for Stripe’s merchants. The Global Payments Performance team serves a critical role both in demonstrating thought leadership on challenging payment topics, and also partnering with our high-potential merchants to set them up for long term success. We want a partnership with Stripe to be a competitive advantage for our customers, large and small, by providing them with best-in-class technology in concert with insightful and specific advice on how to harness this technology to achieve their business goals.

What you’ll do

The Payments Performance EMEA team will be responsible for leading data-driven discussions with existing and prospective merchants on optimisation strategies across a variety of areas including, card network costs, acceptance, fraud, and cross-border flows to start. You will be instrumental in building our optimisation narratives/tools and delivering on our merchant engagement model. You will also collaborate with Sales, deploying your knowledge to differentiate Stripe to win deals, and partner with our Customer Success organization to ensure that merchants are successful working with Stripe.

Responsibilities

  • Lead discussions with existing and prospective merchants, and provide the Sales team with tools and training to lead discussions with merchants and prospects.
  • Serve as both an internal and merchant-facing expert on payment optimisation strategies.
  • Gather and build on Stripe’s wide-ranging payments expertise to create optimisation narratives/tools supported by rigorous analysis.
  • Use existing tools to deploy sophisticated optimisation playbooks and analyses across Stripe’s customer portfolio.
  • Synthesise and relay customer feedback and our findings to inform Stripe’s product roadmap.
  • Provide feedback on our tools and playbooks to help continuously improve our self serve offerings

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 7+ years in payments or operations at a leading technology company, or consultancy in the payments industry. 
  • Understanding of e-commerce payments, cards based payments processing and optimisation strategies
  • A proven ability to build collaborative working relationships with cross-functional teams.
  • The ability to deal effectively with ambiguity and thrive in an unstructured, fast-moving environment.
  • A proven ability to be a self-starter capable of driving business results without significant supervision.
  • Experience presenting directly to merchants and serving as a subject matter expert providing both internal and customer-facing advisory in the payments domain.
  • Develop optimization playbooks and stay updated on industry best practices and Stripe innovations
  • A track record of delivering measurable improvements in payment acceptance, conversion, fraud outcomes or payment costs across a portfolio of underlying merchants or sellers.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong data processing, organizational and analytical skills.
  • Language proficiency in French is essential for this role.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with SQL, dashboard building, modeling, or reporting
  • Understanding of card network rules and regulations, local payment methods, and the regulatory environment (PSD2/PSD3)
  • Experience presenting to senior business leaders
  • Experience working with SaaS Platform or marketplace business models is a plus
  • Familiarity with Stripe Connect or comparable platform-payments solutions, including connected-account models, payment flows, and the allocation of fees and risk responsibilities.

  • Design future anomaly detection systems and tools to ensure that data flowing through our partner and internal systems is reliable and correct

  • Have experience managing communications and workflows with technical and non-technical teams across internal and external stakeholders
  • Ability to write high quality code. We work mostly in Ruby and Java. However, languages can be learned: we care much more about your general coding skill than knowledge of a particular language or framework

  • Be able to build operational processing and tooling from scratch to prevent repeatable issues

  • Great technical problem-solving skills, with an ability to develop a working understanding of a technical system using a variety of methods. These include (but aren't limited to): reading/writing code, reading documentation or partner specifications, running debugging programs, reading logs, asking well-formed questions to domain experts, or digging into the raw data through various interfaces

About Bybit EU

Bybit is one of the world’s leading cryptocurrency exchanges, committed to building a secure, compliant, and transparent digital asset ecosystem. As we expand our regulated European operations from our Vienna headquarters under the MiCA and DORA frameworks, we are looking for an ICT Risk Management Engineer to strengthen our technology resilience, operational risk controls, and regulatory readiness across our European infrastructure.

Role Overview

As an ICT Risk Management Engineer, you will bridge the gap between technical engineering, cybersecurity, and regulatory risk management. You will be helping to identify, assess, and mitigate Information and Communication Technology (ICT) risks across cloud infrastructure, trading systems, and third-party vendors—ensuring our technology stack meets the highest standards of operational resilience and European regulatory compliance (specifically DORA – Digital Operational Resilience Act).

Key Responsibilities

  • ICT Risk Assessments & Control Design: Conduct technical risk assessments across applications, cloud infrastructure, APIs, and core systems; design and implement effective technical controls to mitigate identified vulnerabilities and weaknesses.
  • DORA & Regulatory Compliance: Support and drive technical compliance with European ICT regulatory frameworks, including DORA, PCI DSS and ISO/IEC 27001, translating regulatory mandates into actionable engineering controls.
  • Continuous Monitoring & Governance: Develop risk metrics, risk identification mechanisms, Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), and audit-ready documentation to provide leadership and regulators with clear visibility into our ICT risk posture.
  • Cross-Functional Advisory: Act as a trusted technical advisor to Product, Engineering, Legal, and Compliance teams during new feature launches, architecture reviews, and regulatory inspections.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Experience: 2–4+ years of experience in ICT Risk Management, Information Security Engineering, Technology Audit, or Operational Resilience within banking, fintech, crypto/digital assets, or a Big 4 technology risk practice.
  • Regulatory & Framework Expertise: Hands-on familiarity with DORA, ISO/IEC 27001/27005, NIST CSF, COBIT, or EBA ICT Guidelines.
  • Technical Foundation: Strong understanding of modern cloud architectures (AWS/GCP), network security, access controls (IAM), SDLC security, and resilient distributed systems.
  • Risk & Audit Acumen: Proven ability to conduct technical control testing, manage remediation tracking, and prepare evidence for internal audits or financial supervisory authorities (e.g., FMA).
  • Communication Skills: Fluency in English with the ability to translate complex technical risks into clear, business-focused recommendations for non-technical stakeholders (German is a strong plus).
  • Certifications (Preferred): CISA, CRISC, CISSP, CISM, or ISO 27001 Lead Auditor/Implementer.
  • Work Setup: Ability to work full-time on-site from our Vienna office.
Why Join Us
 
At Bybit, we are committed to fostering a supportive and enriching work environment. Our benefits include:
  • Study Growth Fund: We support your professional development and continuous learning.
  • Internal Events: Participate in regular team-building activities, workshops, and events designed to promote collaboration and innovation.
  • Global Collaboration: Be part of a diverse, international team, working alongside colleagues from around the world.
  • Career Advancement: Access opportunities for growth and advancement within a rapidly expanding global company.

About Paxos

Today’s financial infrastructure is archaic, expensive, inefficient and risky — supporting a system that leaves out more people than it lets in. So we’re rebuilding it.

We’re on a mission to open the world’s financial system to everyone by enabling the instant movement of any asset, any time, in a trustworthy way. For over a decade, we’ve built blockchain infrastructure that tokenizes, custodies, trades and settles assets for the world's leading financial institutions, like PayPal, Venmo, Mastercard, Interactive Brokers and Charles Schwab.

About the team

Product Security works across engineering to secure our applications and services. Partnering closely with engineering, we integrate security into every stage of development, from design documents to code reviews and CI/CD deployment pipelines. Our focus centers on secure defaults, intelligent automation, and pragmatic solutions rather than bureaucracy. We integrate AI tooling into our everyday testing, code review, and workflow automation. Operating within a highly regulated environment, our work safeguards customer trust and regulatory standing, requiring an exceptionally high standard of execution.

About the role

As a Senior Application Security Engineer, you will act as a key security partner across product and engineering teams, taking ownership of threat modeling, architecture reviews, and application code assessments, and supporting smart contract reviews. You will maintain and advance our automated security tooling to detect vulnerabilities early in the development lifecycle. Given our cloud-native infrastructure, you will continuously evaluate application and infrastructure security in tandem, analyzing deployment pipelines, service boundaries, access controls, and identity management. Rather than addressing vulnerabilities individually, you will focus on building scalable guardrails and secure design patterns, balancing robust security controls with product velocity and user experience. You will write code yourself, building the libraries, guardrails, and fixes, and you will be the security lead for the teams you support, mentoring engineers along the way. You will exercise significant autonomy and directly shape the evolution of our Application Security program.

What you'll do

  • Drive security design reviews and threat modeling initiatives for new products and major updates, evaluating both application architecture and cloud deployment strategies.

  • Conduct comprehensive security assessments and secure code reviews on critical APIs and services, targeting business logic, data governance, and authorization mechanisms.

  • Support reviews of blockchain integrations and smart contracts, collaborating closely with engineering teams and third-party auditors to remediate vulnerabilities.

  • Build security guardrails into CI/CD (SAST, SCA, secrets scanning, and supply chain safeguards) and keep findings high-signal to maintain developer trust.

  • Triage and prioritize security findings from bug bounties, penetration tests, and automated scanners based on contextual risk, steering them to resolution.

  • Write code: build the libraries, guardrails, and fixes yourself instead of handing findings back to teams.

  • Establish secure-by-default architecture, reusable libraries, and best-practice frameworks to systematically resolve entire classes of security vulnerabilities.

  • Partner with cloud security specialists to enforce application-level controls, including service identity management, network segmentation, and secrets handling.

  • Leverage AI platforms to automate workflows, accelerate review and triage capabilities, and expand program impact.

  • Assist in incident response efforts for application-layer events and lead post-incident security strengthening initiatives.

  • Act as the security lead for the teams you support, and provide actionable security guidance and mentorship to engineering teams to foster a culture of secure development.

About you

  • 5+ years combined in software engineering and application security, including hands-on experience building and shipping production software

  • Strong software development and secure code review skills in at least one of Go, Java, Python, or TypeScript, with the ability to quickly evaluate unfamiliar codebases

  • Practical expertise in threat modeling as well as web and API security, specifically targeting business logic, authentication, and authorization vulnerabilities

  • Demonstrated experience securing cloud-native applications (preferably AWS), covering containers and Kubernetes, IAM, secrets management, service-to-service authentication, and CI/CD pipelines

  • Proven ability to scale security mitigation using secure design patterns, automated tooling, and shared frameworks

  • Track record of implementing and fine-tuning CI/CD automated security scanners to minimize noise and false positives

  • Basic understanding of cryptography and blockchain; applied cryptography or hands-on smart contract audit experience is a plus

  • Regular adoption of AI coding and static analysis tools for development and auditing, alongside an informed perspective on their effective application

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills to collaborate effectively with software engineers, product management, and engineering leadership

  • Proven history of partnering with engineering teams to resolve security vulnerabilities rather than simply cataloging them

  • Experience mentoring engineers and acting as the security lead for an area

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience

Important Notice for Paxos Applicants
Fraudulent accounts sometimes pose as Paxos recruiters on LinkedIn and other platforms, and fake websites sometimes impersonate our careers site. These scammers attempt to deceive applicants into paying for job opportunities or providing personal financial information.

To verify a legitimate Paxos opportunity:

  • Our only official careers site is paxos.com/careers

  • We only use @paxos.com email addresses

  • We never ask for payment or financial details to apply, interview, or work here

  • For technical roles, we do not perform a coding interview without prior screening by our engineering team

Thanks for your interest in Paxos!

Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

In one line

Our team builds the platform that every TRM product, every internal AI agent, and every investigation our customers run depends on. We are not maintaining a system someone else finished - we are building its next generation, on the bleeding edge, for workloads where reliability and security are not negotiable. We're looking for an engineer who has taken infrastructure from zero to one and can operate it in production.

Why this work matters

TRM's platform lets financial institutions and governments trace illicit finance, disrupt crypto- and AI-enabled crime, and run some of the highest-stakes investigations in the world. Our infrastructure is what lets investigators and banks trust the data underneath them. When we get it right, a case moves and a threat gets stopped. When infrastructure is weak, everything above it is slow, fragile, or unsafe. That's the job: make the foundation something the mission can be built on.

What you'll actually work on

This is real, current work - not a hypothetical roadmap:

  • Multi-region, multi-cloud Kubernetes across US GCP, EU GCP, and AWS GovCloud - making "stand up another site" a self-serve configuration instead of a bespoke project.

  • A genuinely self-serve internal PaaS. ~60+ engineers already deploy on it, the large majority with no infra person in the loop. You extend the paved road - golden paths, guardrails, and interfaces engineers actually enjoy using.

  • Agent-native infrastructure. Secure sandboxes where AI agents build and ship, and encoding our operational knowledge into skills so the platform increasingly runs and heals itself.

  • Zero-trust secrets with Vault. Short-lived, dynamic credentials replacing every long-lived secret in the system - closing the blast radius on leaked passwords, one database at a time.

  • Reliability engineering that means it. SLOs and error budgets, real observability, and disaster recovery with validated cross-region restore and sub-hour RTO.

  • Databases as a first-class platform concern. Postgres on Kubernetes, migrations, replication, and redundancy for services that can't blink.

  • Compliance as code. SOC2 and FedRAMP posture built into the platform so security is the default, not a scramble before an audit.

What you'll own

You'll own an Area of Responsibility end to end - a slice of the platform that is genuinely yours. You'll define what "great" looks like for it and build the glide path to get there rather than waiting for one; obsess over the metrics that tell you whether it's actually working; and fix root causes so a class of problems disappears instead of working the ticket queue faster. You own the outcome, not just your layer of it.

Who you are

This is a builder's role, and the bar is high:

  • You've taken infrastructure from zero to one - designed and shipped a platform capability that other engineers came to depend on, not just operated one that already existed.

  • You write real software (Go, Python, or similar). You build tooling, automation, and services - you don't only wire up other people's tools.

  • You're deep in GCP and/or AWS - compute, IAM, VPC, networking, storage, load balancing - and comfortable operating across clouds.

  • You've run Kubernetes in production (GKE/EKS) and are up to date with the state of the art for IaC.

  • You can debug low-level problems without hand-holding - a networking issue, a saturated node, a slow query, a failing deploy - and get to the actual cause.

  • You're fluent across the modern platform toolchain: GitOps (Argo/Flux), containers, CI/CD, observability built on SLOs rather than dashboards no one reads.

  • You have strong instincts for security and databases — zero-trust, secret management, systems hardening; provisioning and migrating production databases. SOC2/FedRAMP exposure is a plus.

If you've built platforms that other engineers rely on every day, we want to talk.

What makes people thrive here

High ownership and low ego. Mission-first. Comfortable where speed and rigor have to coexist - something that takes a quarter elsewhere is expected to move in weeks here, without cutting the corners that matter for security and reliability. You see infra, security, data, and product as one connected system, and you turn one-off fixes into reusable paved roads by instinct.

What should give you pause

The scope is real and the playbook isn't fully written - you'll be writing it. Reliability and compliance expectations are high, and mistakes here show up as real incidents for customers and internal teams. If you prefer an environment where everything is defined before you start, this will feel uncomfortable. If that kind of ownership is exactly what you're after, you'll love it.

How we work

Remote-first (US). Small, high-leverage team with a weekly on-call rotation you'll take part in. We're an AI-native team in practice, not in theory - we use agents in our daily workflow and ship the skills that let the platform operate itself.

The estimated base salary range for this role and level is $205,000 - $245,000

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

About Morpho

Morpho is a leading Decentralized Finance (DeFi) lending protocol backed by a16z crypto, Paradigm, Ribbit Capital, Apollo, Vaneck, Coinbase Ventures, Variant and 50 others to build an open credit network giving anyone, anywhere, access to the best possible terms. Morpho is experiencing exponential adoption, with over billion in deposits on the network and used by institutional clients including Bitwise, Galaxy, and Anchorage Digital and the largest crypto exchanges, such as Coinbase, Binance, and Kraken. Now, Morpho is scaling its team of contributors to establish itself as the open credit network, not just of DeFi, but of the world.

 

Why Morpho Exists

Everyone has the potential to build something great for the world. But fulfilling that ambition almost always requires more: people willing to trust you with their capital. Yet access to capital still depends on where you live, who you know, and which institutions are willing to trust you. Even when capital is available, it sits fragmented across disconnected networks and hidden behind intermediaries. The result is a system that fails most of the people it should serve. Borrowers overpay. Lenders earn less than they should. Many are shut out entirely, not because they are unworthy of credit, but because today's infrastructure was never built to connect them. Morpho exists to solve this. Full article here.

Location

New York preferred. Remote is possible between GMT-5 and GMT+2.

 

Role

Banks, asset managers and token issuers are bringing stocks, funds and other real-world assets onchain. Those assets become far more useful once their holders can borrow against them and lend them out. Midnight, Morpho's fixed-rate, fixed-term lending protocol, gives institutions the predictable terms they need to do that.

 

This role owns the products that make Morpho the credit layer for institutional assets, spanning tokenized equities and funds as collateral, loans backed by assets held with a qualified custodian, and the onchain equivalents of repo and securities lending.

 

Close partnership with institutions is central to this role. You will develop a detailed understanding of how they operate across trading, custody and compliance, and translate their requirements into products that scale across many partners.

 

Responsibilities

 

  • Own the vision, strategy and roadmap for institutional credit on Morpho, end to end.

  • Act as Morpho's domain expert on the institutional market. Go deep with issuers, asset managers, banks, custodians and brokers on how they finance and lend assets, represent Morpho with them, and turn conflicting input into precise problem statements and requirements.

  • Decide which issuers and asset types come first, which wait and which Morpho declines, and make the trade-offs explicit.

  • Judge which partner-specific requests become standard capabilities many institutions can use, and make the build or partner call for each.

  • Work as a peer to the protocol team on design trade-offs, bringing legal and risk in early on custody, transfer restrictions, valuation and liquidation for each asset type.

  • Drive each initiative from problem definition through launch and adoption, across teams you do not manage. Define success before launch, measured in active loans.

 

What Success Looks Like

 

First 30 days

You understand Morpho's lending stack and what Midnight makes possible. You have met protocol, markets, vaults, solutions, business development and legal, and joined live conversations with issuers and asset managers. You have written down where the issuer product stands and what blocks its first launch.

 

First 3 months

The first issuers are onboarding to a defined product with standard terms. You have a ranked view of the next two institutional loan types, backed by partner evidence, with named partners in conversation for each.

 

First 6 months

Issuers are live and holders of their assets are borrowing. A second institutional loan type has a working proof of concept with real counterparties. New institutions onboard through a repeatable process, not a custom project.

 

Must Have Experience & Skills

  • Shipped products for institutional users in capital markets or securities finance: repo, securities lending, prime brokerage, collateral management, custody or tokenized assets.

  • A track record of taking a product from zero to one, where you found the opportunity and carried it through launch.

  • Working knowledge of how institutions hold, finance and lend assets, and of the regulatory and operational constraints that shape those products.

  • Comfortable leading conversations with senior people at banks, asset managers and issuers, and turning them into clear requirements.

  • Able to deliver through influence across teams, without a dedicated engineering team.

  • Clear writing and speaking for technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Creates clarity and drives decisions in ambiguous situations, and acts without waiting to be told.

  • Team-first mindset, low ego.

 

Nice to Have

  • Experience with onchain lending, tokenization or digital asset custody.

  • Time on both sides: at a traditional financial institution and at a technology company.

  • Has been a founder, or owned a new product line end to end.

Perks & Benefits

We design benefits around deep work and growth, so you can do the best work of your career. Expect fair, top-tier compensation, real flexibility, time together in Paris, great health coverage, and support to keep learning.

 

Equal Opportunity

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and hire based on talent, potential, and values alignment.

You will turn accounting requirements into scalable, auditable, self-service platform capabilities that product, engineering, finance, and compliance can build on. 

Digital assets make this harder, and more interesting, than it is at a traditional bank. On chain activity, custody structures, staking, tokenized assets, and settlement each move through our systems differently, and each has to land correctly on the books. The industry is still writing the playbook for much of this. You will help write it. 

Level 

We are hiring at Senior or Principal level, depending on experience. The core scope is the same at both. At Principal, you have already set platform strategy, led accounting systems, or established control standards that multiple teams adopted, and you will own the crossproduct standards and the working relationship with finance and audit leadership with more independence from day one.

Two paths to this role 

There is more than one way to be great at this job. You may come from product management and built financial compliance platforms. You may come from audit, controllership, or accounting systems and have spent years finding where numbers break, and then built the thing that fixed it. We are just as interested in the second group. If you are an auditor or accountant with a builder mindset, you will be evaluated on the same scope and the same bar as a product manager. What matters is that you have shipped: tools, automation, control frameworks, or systems that other teams adopted and kept using.

What you will own 

  • The financial data and accounting platform roadmap: Define and deliver the shared capabilities that make financial data trustworthy by construction: ledger and sub-ledger integrity, balance and activity reconciliation, fee and revenue calculation, client reporting, and the feeds into the general ledger and the financial close. 
  • Controls built into the product: Partner with finance, internal audit, and external auditors to turn SOX and internal control requirements into product capabilities instead of manual procedures. When a control needs a build, you own the requirements, the plan, and the timeline, delivered in step with the audit calendar. 
  • Platform standards across products and entities: Make sure new products, new asset types, new legal entities, and acquisitions plug into the platform instead of creating bespoke accounting workarounds. You set the standards, interfaces, and data contracts that product teams build against. 
  • Regulatory and audit readiness: Work with compliance, legal, and risk so the platform supports regulatory reporting, books-and-records requirements, and examiner and auditor requests. You run dated plans against external deadlines and flag early when a timeline is at risk. 
  • Close, reporting, and operational efficiency: Reduce the manual effort, elapsed time, and risk in month-end and quarter-end close. Establish the metrics that show whether the platform is working: reconciliation breaks, close duration, audit adjustments, manual journal volume, and time to onboard a new product. 

What success looks like in the first two quarters 

  • A documented map of how each major product's financial activity reaches the general ledger, with manual steps and gaps identified and prioritized. 
  • A dated platform roadmap agreed with finance, engineering, and compliance, with external deadlines (audit, regulatory, and reporting) built into the plan. 
  • One high-impact capability shipped end to end, such as automated reconciliation for a key product, that measurably reduces manual work or control risk. 

Who you will partner with 

  • Finance and Accounting leadership own accounting policy and judgment. You translate their requirements into platform capabilities and make the product the system of record. 
  • Engineering leadership owns architecture, estimates, and delivery. You partner on sequencing, platform design, and tradeoffs without positional authority. Product Managers across Custody, Trading, Staking, and Financing need the platform to support their products without becoming a bottleneck. 
  • Compliance, Legal, and Risk own regulatory judgment. You build the delivery process behind it. 
  • Internal and external audit rely on you to plan control-related work clearly and deliver it on schedule. 
  • Commercial and client teams need accurate statements, reporting, and billing that clients can trust. 

What we're looking for 

  • 6+ years of experience (typically 9+ for Principal) building or scaling systems, platforms, tooling, or control frameworks that multiple internal or external teams relied on, including 3+ years as the owner. You might have done this as a product manager, or from audit, controllership, or accounting systems. At Principal, you have set strategy or standards that other teams adopted.
  • An accounting or finance foundation: a CPA or equivalent, an accounting degree, or hands-on experience in financial reporting, audit, controllership, or accounting systems. You can read a trial balance, follow a journal entry through a ledger, and discuss revenue recognition or reconciliation with a controller without a translator.
  • Experience building scalable platforms such as ledgers, billing, payments, reporting, data infrastructure, reconciliation tooling, or controls automation. You think in data models, interfaces, and reuse, and you know when a one-off fix will cost us later. If you come from audit or accounting, this may look like automating reconciliations, building controls into a system, or designing data models and tooling with engineers, rather than a formal product title.
  • Experience in a regulated financial environment. You have worked with auditors, examiners, SOX controls, or control programs, and you understand how public company obligations change how products are built and shipped.
  • Technical credibility with Engineers. You can follow an architecture discussion, pressure-test an estimate, and write precise requirements for data-heavy systems. Familiarity with SQL and financial data pipelines is a plus.
  • Crypto or digital-asset experience is a requirement. If you do not have professional experience, passion projects with breadth and depth across digital assets could be a good fit.
  • A writing-first approach: your default artifacts are clear specs, data flow maps, and decision documents.

What will make you fail here 

  • Building bespoke solutions for each product or blockchain instead of platform capabilities that scale. 
  • Needing positional authority to get things done. Engineering, finance, and compliance sit on separate reporting lines, and you will coordinate across all three every day. You need to find ways to unblock yourself. 
  • Optimizing for process over outcomes. We have little patience for ceremony. Here, a control built into the product is an outcome; a new manual review step usually isn't. 

Why Join BitGo?

Disrupting an industry takes vision, innovation, passion, technical chops, drive to deliver, collaboration, and execution. Join a team of great people who strive for excellence and personify our corporate values of ownership, craftsmanship, and open communication. We are looking for new colleagues who bring innovative ways of thinking and problem-solving, and who want risks to be part of the team that changes the world’s financial markets.

Depending upon your leveling and location, the compensation for this role averages between $230,000 and $260,000 USD base salary. Equity, an annual performance bonus, and the benefits outlined above are also part of this role’s package.

Position Responsibilities

  • Lead the strategy and evolution of Talks at GS, refining programming priorities, editorial themes, and identifying new opportunities to strengthen the franchise globally
  • Build and manage a robust global guest pipeline, identifying timely and distinctive voices across categories
  • Align content development with firm-wide themes, target audiences, and divisional priorities
  • Lead guest vetting, outreach, and booking, partnering with senior stakeholders across the firm and external talent management
  • Set the editorial direction and scripting for each conversation; oversee moderator and guest preparation and editorial approvals
  • Oversee end-to-end pre- and post-production, shaping long- and short-form video, social, audio, and digital assets
  • Develop go-to-market, distribution, and amplification strategies, in partnership with content strategy and brand marketing partners
  • Proactively build trusted relationships and scalable operating models across the firm, partnering with senior leaders, control functions, vendors, and production teams to assess current and future content needs
  • Oversee budgets and vendor relationships
  • Manage a small team of full-time/contingent junior producers and project managers
  • Stay ahead of the competitive and thought leadership landscape, innovating best-in-class content products that position Goldman Sachs as a global thought leader

Additional competencies, knowledge, and experiences required for this role include

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • 7+ years of experience in content strategy and execution, with a proven track record of leading live events and experiences end-to-end
  • Experience in financial and business media and/or the financial services industry preferred
  • Sound editorial judgement and risk-management orientation
  • Awareness of and interest in emerging trends within the content and product landscape
  • Data-driven, performance-oriented mindset
  • Collaborative, hands-on work approach and ability to work well across a dynamic global team
  • Superior attention to detail

Salary Range
